# Independent derivation, saved before reading the paired prover

2026-10-10. Worker w382. Only the target ranking and Chatterjee Theorem 1.1 have been used here; no w381 or w383 proof has been read. This is an obstruction to an abstract implication, not an iid FPP construction and not a solution of P0110.

For n >= 2, let B_n be Bernoulli(n^(-1/2)) and let C_n be Bernoulli(n^(-1/4)). No independence across n or between these two families is needed. Define centered X_n = n^(1/2)(B_n - n^(-1/2)) and nonnegative D_n = n^(3/4) C_n.

Define chi_a as the infimum of s for which some alpha > 0 makes sup_n E exp(alpha |X_n|/n^s) finite, and chi_b as the supremum of s for which inf_{n>N} Var(X_n)/n^(2s) > 0 for some N. Define xi_a with D_n in place of |X_n| in the exponential bound and xi_b with E D_n/n^s in the lower bound.

Then chi_a = 1/2, chi_b = 1/4, xi_a = 3/4, xi_b = 1/2.

Proof: |X_n| <= n^(1/2) and D_n <= n^(3/4), which give the upper exponential bounds at their stated endpoints. For s < 1/2 the event B_n=1 contributes at least n^(-1/2) exp(alpha n^(1/2-s)/2) to the X exponential moment for n >= 4; this tends to infinity for every alpha > 0. Likewise C_n=1 contributes n^(-1/4) exp(alpha n^(3/4-s)), which diverges for every s < 3/4 and every alpha > 0. Finally Var(X_n) = n^(1/2)(1-n^(-1/2)) and E D_n = n^(1/2), so the two lower endpoints are exactly 1/4 and 1/2.

Thus a polynomial variance exponent, a polynomial expected-deviation exponent, boundedness at the generic allowed scales, and even chi_a = 2 xi_a - 1 do not imply equality of the two definitions for either exponent. Strong uniform exponential-tail information at the claimed smaller scale is missing. This scalar example is not FPP; it refutes only the inference from moment data to matching exponential-moment exponents without further structure.

The hardest open bridge for the Chatterjee route is to find one genuine iid nearest-neighbor FPP law on Z^d, d >= 2, for which both equalities of upper and lower exponents hold. Known-law admissibility alone does not supply that bridge. Full target record and survey question still to be recovered.

Independent check required from w383. The arguments above do not multiply conditional bounds or assume independent geodesic increments.
remaining_gap: Independent referee check; no iid FPP realization or target closure.

statement: A supporting-sphere direction of a norm does not imply a positive quadratic detour bound in every direction. For g(x)=||x||_1 on R^2, n a positive multiple of four, v=(n,n), z=(3n/4,n/4), g(z)+g(v-z)-g(v)=0 while dist(z,[0,v])=n/(2sqrt(2)). Therefore a bound c dist(z,[0,v])^2/|v|-K with c>0 and finite K cannot hold uniformly in n and direction just from the norm axioms. This geometry example does not assert that an eligible continuous iid FPP law has this shape. Independent referee check is pending.

proof_or_counterexample:
# Directional exponential-moment upgrade of the complete finite-scale tail

Draft conditional deduction, w382, 2026-10-10. Independent referee required: w383. This is not a solution of P0110 and is not a global exponent claim.

Use w381 L1--L5's exact assumptions and notation: fixed d>=2, iid edge weights in [a,b] with 0<a<b<infinity, g the time-constant norm, rho=min_{|u|=1}g(u)>0, u a minimizing unit vector, v_n nearest-integer rounding of nu for integer n>=sqrt(d), L_n=|v_n|, C=(b/a)sqrt(d), K0=bd/2+rho sqrt(d)/2, and D_n the largest distance to [0,v_n] over all minimizing paths. Suppose q>=0, alpha>0, K>=1 and, for every nonzero lattice w, E exp(alpha |T(0,w)-h(w)|/|w|^q)<=K. Also suppose B_n=h(v_n)-g(v_n)<=H n^q log(2+n) with a finite H>=0. All constants are fixed in n.

Let A_n=2|{z in Z^d: ||z||_1<=(b/a)||v_n||_1}|+1 and Q_n=((C+1)L_n)^q/alpha. L5 gives, for each t>=0,

P(D_n>sqrt(U_n+V_n t))<=exp(-t),

where U_n=C L_n (B_n+K0+3 Q_n log(A_n K))/(2rho) and V_n=3 C L_n Q_n/(2rho)>0. This is obtained by taking s=Q_n(log(A_n K)+t). The logarithm is nonnegative because A_n K>=1.

Set Y_n=((D_n-sqrt(U_n))_+)^2/V_n. Since sqrt(U_n)+sqrt(V_n t)>=sqrt(U_n+V_n t), P(Y_n>t)<=exp(-t). For a nonnegative random variable with this tail, the layer-cake identity gives E exp(Y_n/2) = 1+(1/2) integral_0^infinity exp(t/2) P(Y_n>t) dt <=2.

For every lambda>0 and r>(1+q)/2, D_n<=sqrt(U_n)+sqrt(V_n Y_n) and ab<=a^2/2+b^2/2 imply

E exp(lambda D_n/n^r) <= 2 exp(lambda sqrt(U_n)/n^r + lambda^2 V_n/(2 n^(2r))).

Indeed apply the elementary inequality with a=lambda sqrt(V_n)/n^r and b=sqrt(Y_n). Since L_n is comparable to n and A_n=O(n^d), U_n=O(n^(1+q) log(2+n)) and V_n=O(n^(1+q)). The right side is bounded uniformly in n for every fixed lambda and r>(1+q)/2. Hence the exponential upper wandering endpoint along this rounded support direction is at most (1+q)/2.

The strict epsilon in r is needed to absorb sqrt(log n); no endpoint claim is made. The proof uses the entire tail for all t, not only a family of polynomial-probability bounds at one threshold. It uses no independence, random conditioning or multiplication of conditional estimates. It gives neither a lower wandering endpoint nor uniform control in all directions. Independent referee w383 must check the new assertion before any theorem promotion.
remaining_gap: Independent referee check; directional and conditional. Does not prove exponent matching.

# Independent adversary review for w381 and w383

2026-10-10. w382. Independent obstruction saved in INDEPENDENT_OBSTRUCTION.md before reading w381/ATTEMPT.md. This review concerns L1--L5 in that file, headed 'terminal-bias bridge, with a supporting sphere'. It is not a review of w383's review.

Verdict: KEEP as conditional finite-scale deductions. No counterexample to L1--L5 was found. These deductions do not solve P0110. The remaining premise for a Chatterjee/Auffinger--Damron closure is matching both global exponent pairs for one eligible nondegenerate iid law. A suitable law's admissibility and a directional upper bound do not establish that premise.

L1 and L2, separately derived: translation invariance and subadditivity give h(mx)<=m h(x), hence g(x)<=h(x). For a vertex z of a minimizing path, T(0,v)=T(0,z)+T(z,v). Substitute T(x,y)=g(y-x)+b(y-x)+X(x,y) and rearrange. The detour equals b(v)-b(z)-b(v-z)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v). Since both internal biases are nonnegative, only the terminal bias must be bounded from above. Signs are correct.

L3, separately derived: for projection inside the segment, S>=sqrt(L^2+4r^2), so S-L>=4r^2/(S+L)>=2r^2/S. For projection outside, the distance to the nearer endpoint is r, and the distance to the farther endpoint is at least L AND at least r. The first fact gives S-L>=r; the second gives S>=2r. Thus S-L>=2r^2/S. The farther-endpoint distance >=L is the small missing explanation in w381's prose, not a missing hypothesis or a counterexample. This handles overshoots as well as perpendicular departures.

L4, separately checked: minimizing g on the Euclidean unit sphere gives rho>0, g(x)>=rho|x| and g(u)=rho for at least one unit vector u. Since g(x)<=b||x||_1, rounding nu contributes at most bd/2 to g(v_n), and ||v_n|-n|<=sqrt(d)/2. Thus g(v_n)-rho|v_n| is between zero and K0. The bounded positive edge law gives a deterministic maximum length (b/a)||v_n||_1 for EVERY minimizing path. Their vertices satisfy S<=C|v_n|, C=(b/a)sqrt(d). Combining these facts with L3 gives the stated lower quadratic detour minus K0.

L5, separately checked: all possible vertices lie in deterministic Lambda_n. Translation invariance permits applying the same centered exponential bound to X(0,z) and X(z,v_n). Distances are <=(C+1)|v_n|, so q>=0 makes the envelope denominator valid. There are at most 2|Lambda_n|+1 terms. A union bound works despite dependence. No bound is conditioned on z being a selected geodesic vertex. L2 and L4 yield the threshold and exponent exactly as written. Zero-displacement terms vanish. If a=b the geometry proof still works, but the degenerate law is excluded as a P0110 witness. If a=0 the deterministic length argument requires a new premise and this proof does not apply.

Two concrete failed closure routes:

1. Moment estimates alone cannot imply matching uniform exponential upper and moment lower exponents. INDEPENDENT_OBSTRUCTION.md gives exact scalar endpoints (1/2,1/4,3/4,1/2). It is a counterexample to that abstract implication, not to iid FPP.
2. Existence of a supporting direction cannot be promoted to a curvature bound in every direction. In R^2 set g=||.||_1, v=(n,n), z=(n/2+r,n/2-r), 0<r<n/2. Then g(z)+g(v-z)-g(v)=0 but dist(z,[0,v])=sqrt(2)r>0. Thus no positive quadratic lower detour bound is uniform over directions merely because g is a norm. The norm example does not assert an eligible continuous iid FPP law has this shape.

Additional conditional deduction for referee w383: CONDITIONAL_EXPONENTIAL_UPGRADE.md converts the full L5 tail to a uniform exponential moment along v_n at every exponent strictly above (1+q)/2. It still supplies no global matching or lower bound. It is an original derivation in this packet and remains unreviewed.

NEXT: w383 independently check the rare-tail obstruction and exponential upgrade; if retaining the conditional route, isolate the global lower/upper matching premise rather than replace it with a variance limit.

statement: For d>=2 and weights in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<3a, every geodesic between adjacent vertices is the direct edge, so D(0,e_1)=0. Consequently inf_{v!=0} E D(0,v)/|v|^s=0 for every real s. Thus Uniform[1,2] fails the literally printed Auffinger--Damron Eq. (2.2) lower wandering premise over all nonzero displacements; this finite obstruction does not refute Chatterjee's lower premise outside a large ball.
assumptions: D is distance to the endpoint segment, maximized over minimizing paths
proof_or_counterexample:
# Printed lower-exponent convention versus a bounded law

Draft exact boundary-case derivation, w382, 2026-10-10. Independent referee w383 must check it. This does not compute an asymptotic exponent and does not settle P0110.

Let d>=2 and let every nearest-neighbor edge weight be in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<3a. In particular, iid Uniform[1,2] meets this condition. For any adjacent vertices x,y, the direct edge has passage time at most b. Every alternative path has at least three edges: the lattice is bipartite, and a path between neighbors has odd length. Positive weights remove any advantage from loops. Every alternative therefore has passage time at least 3a>b. The unique minimizing path is the direct edge for every environment in this support class.

Consequently D(0,e_1)=0, where D is the maximum distance from any minimizing path to the segment [0,e_1]. Thus for every real s,

inf_{v in Z^d except 0} E D(0,v)/|v|^s = 0.

As literally printed, Auffinger--Damron arXiv:1109.0523v2 equation (2.2), PDF page 4, requires that infimum to be strictly positive for each exponent below xi_b. No real xi_b can satisfy that printed all-nonzero-displacements convention for Uniform[1,2]. This is a failed hypothesis application, not a contradiction of their conditional theorem.

Chatterjee's published Theorem 1.1 instead requires its lower estimates only outside a sufficiently large ball. The finite adjacent-vertex obstruction does not contradict that asymptotic convention. Uniform[1,2] belongs to the nearly-gamma class named by that theorem, so it is possible to choose Chatterjee's exact sufficient route without silently weakening the printed Auffinger--Damron premise. Matching the asymptotic global exponent pairs is still unproved here.

Review implication: w381 L1--L5 remain valid for Uniform[1,2], but 'eligible law' should mean the weight-support assumptions only, not all the global-exponent assumptions of the printed Auffinger--Damron statement. A modified lower-bound convention needs explicit justification before invoking that theorem; using Chatterjee's stated large-distance convention keeps the theorem statement intact.

Primary references: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.0523 Eq. (2.2); https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v177-n2-p07-p.pdf Theorem 1.1, (A4).
remaining_gap: Independent referee check; no asymptotic exponent matching has been shown. Do not silently modify a published theorem's assumptions.
